system.summary: Plain Chinese standard telegraph code (four-digit codes), no encipherment, read in typing order. (The Dalai Lama's replies in the same file, pp. 9, 11, 12, 22-23, are in pronounceable 5-letter code words, CVCVC and VCVCV joined in pairs, probably from a codebook; they are not part of this reading: see NOTES.md and outcome.gaps.)
system.notes: Date codes (韻目): 元 = 13th, 庚 = 8th.

prior_solution.where: In the archive, an abstract only: Foreign and Political Department to Weir, D.O. 29 Sept 1930 (same file p. 18), an English abstract of the Nanking messages (Chiang received the Dalai Lama's letter through Kun Kanpu; China had not been 'honest or considerate'; complete unity; greetings from Ma Fuxiang and Kun Kanpu); no translation and no Chinese text. Web search 11 Nov 2026 and two at verification (12 Nov 2026): nothing printed. Chinese printed document collections were not searched.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the target, logged in to Abhilekh Patal and captured the pages, and set the rules (protocol hashed before the attack; every decipherment goes to Daniel). A Claude Opus 5.5 agent checked the groups, wrote the protocol, read the telegrams, ran the controls and wrote up. Integration (12 Nov 2026): the decoding and the controls were re-run for the project with an independent decoder and Unihan table; the images were not seen (the archive shows a human check to scripts).

solution.what: File seen after login on Abhilekh Patal (NAIDLF03824535); pp. 9-23 captured; OCR text layer of pp. 9-15 read.
Lead 1359 status (open); web search on the 1930 Nanking-Lhasa telegrams: nothing printed.

Protocol hashed before the attack, by the contributor's record (frozen/PREREG.md, SHA-256 23aba69b...): plain standard telegraph code first; additives and the 1908 General Staff formula held in reserve. Plain code worked at once on pp. 14-15.

Controls with a crib changed after decoding (frozen/controles_A.py has 棍堪布 and 誠 and drops 貢覺仲尼, 貢覺, 堪布, 誠意 and 函 of the protocol's list): crib words of two or more characters 14 (p. 14) and 10 (p. 15) against max 4 and 3 over 1,000 random orders of the groups; 1,000 random 4-digit additives max 2 (frozen/controles_A.out). Both halves of each telegram read. With the crib actually fixed in the protocol (rerun at verification, 12 Nov 2026): 12 and 9 against max 4 and 3.

p. 14: 150 codes as written + 3 emended by one digit + 2 unresolved of 155; p. 15: 71 + 3 + 1 of 75. By the read bar (emended codes not counted): 96.8% and 94.7%, 221 of 230 = 96.1%. The contributor counted the emended codes as read: 227 of 230 = 98.7%.

Code words (pp. 9, 11, 12): structure found (5-letter words CVCVC/VCVCV, shared opening and closing words between pp. 11 and 12). A syllable-to-digit-pair table (word = CTC number + filler letter), tried with the guess that the shared closing words spell 達賴喇嘛, is inconsistent; alphabetical rank of the words gives nothing. No crib (the p. 18 abstract covers the Nanking telegrams, not these). The held-out message (p. 9), designated in the protocol, was never used: no key, no measurement.

Integration of PR #434 after an independent verification: a separate decoder with a code table built from Unihan.zip (same SHA-256) gives the claimed character for all 221 codes read as written; the nine exceptions are the six one-digit emendations and three unresolved codes listed. frozen/controles_A.py rerun gives controles_A.out byte for byte. Finding: the control crib is not the protocol's crib (changed after decoding); with the protocol's crib the scores are 12 (p. 14) and 9 (p. 15) against max 4 and 3 over 1,000 random orders, and over all non-zero 4-digit additives the best scores 5 and 3 against 14 and 11 for the plain reading. Corrections: read share by the read bar 221/230 = 96.1% (p. 15 71/75 = 94.7%, read in part), class 'already solved' -> 'read in part', provenance 'mixed' -> 'contributed', 4158 目 added as a candidate for 4156, the 8th/13th ordering problem recorded, the OCR source of the transcription stated. Not done: no image was seen (Abhilekh Patal shows a human check to scripts; not gone round); Chinese printed collections not searched.

outcome.method_basis: The key is the public Chinese standard telegraph code (table from Unicode Unihan); the telegrams are not enciphered. No Chinese text or translation existed: the file of 1930 holds an English abstract only.
outcome.fraction_read_source: By the read bar, counting only codes that give the character as written and read as sense: p. 14 150 of 155 (96.8%), p. 15 71 of 75 (94.7%), 221/230 = 96.1%. Not counted: six codes emended by one digit and three unresolved. (The contributor's figure, with the emended codes counted: 227/230 = 98.7%.) The code-word telegrams (pp. 9, 11, 12, 22-23) are another system, not read and not counted.

texts.label: p. 14: Chiang Kai-shek to the Dalai Lama, September 1930 (the 13th)
texts.summary: Chiang Kai-shek thanks the Dalai Lama for the letter, replies on eight points, photograph and gifts brought by Kun Kanpu; admits that past rulers did not treat Tibet with sincerity; welcomes his support of the central government; China and Tibet one family, unification completed; Ma Fuxiang instructed to handle the matter.

reading_review.by: integration review for the project (independent verification, then the integrator)
reading_review.note: Read as formal epistolary Chinese from end to end: opening on Kun Kanpu's audience, 中藏關係本極密切 ... 不以真誠相見, 從此中藏一家，完成統一, closing 並祝健康, signature 蔣中正 and date code 元. 150 codes as written, 3 emended by one digit, 2 unresolved (慧?明心, and one group before the signature). First read by the contributor's agent on 11 Nov 2026. No sinologist has re-read it, and the transcription (from an OCR text layer) was not checked against the image.

texts.label: p. 15: Ma Fuxiang to the Dalai Lama, September 1930 (the 8th)
texts.summary: Ma Fuxiang, after more than twenty years apart, has met Kun Kanpu; Chairman Chiang praises the Dalai Lama's support of the central government and has answered by telegram; Ma will handle his affairs with devotion. Three words rest on one-digit emendations and one code is unresolved.

reading_review.by: integration review for the project (independent verification, then the integrator)
reading_review.note: Read as a letter-telegram: 暌違廿餘載，馳念良殷 opening, 敬祝嘉福 closing, signature 馬福祥, date code 庚. Coherent throughout; 71 codes as written, 3 emended by one digit (蔣, 許, 竭), 1 unresolved (公私兩?), which puts the telegram at 94.7%, under the read bar. First read by the contributor's agent on 11 Nov 2026. No sinologist has re-read it, and the transcription (from an OCR text layer) was not checked against the image.

outcome.notes: No image of the NAI file is included (no reuse licence shown; the site shows a human check to scripts). Not a first break: the Government of India summarised these two telegrams in 1930. New here: the Chinese texts and translations. The Dalai Lama's code-word replies in the same file are another system and remain unread. outcome.key is 'not applicable', as in targets/ctcplain1913: the key is a public table and nothing was recovered; the nine odd codes are slips in the text or its transcription, not holes in the key.
